title: Bellarmine and Becanus especially fasten these charges; this disputation answers by Reformed sense
source_text: II. Istud praesertim videre est apud Bellarminum & Becanum Jesuitas, qui talia vel supponunt, vel etiam diserte & expresse nobis affingunt, in suis contra nos Disputationibus. Cum ergo Thesibus nostris praecedentibus de Justificatione, & quaestionibus annexis, multas jam ejusmodi calumnias discussimus nuda & perspicua veritatis expositione; juxta Doctorum Reformatorum sensum, his quoque consimili modo occurrere visum est praesenti Disputatione.
pass_a_gloss: This is seen especially in Bellarmine and Becanus the Jesuits, who either assume such things or even expressly and openly fasten them upon us in their disputations against us. Since therefore in our preceding theses on justification and the annexed questions we have already shaken off many such calumnies by a bare and clear exposition of the truth, it has seemed good, according to the sense of the Reformed doctors, to meet these likewise in a similar way by the present disputation.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine and Becanus especially pin these charges on the Reformed.
This disputation answers them by the same clear exposition already used on justification.
